title: War of the Third Coalition (1798–1802)
key_facts: Second Coalition (Britain, Austria, Russia, Ottoman Empire) fought against France
French campaigns in Switzerland and Germany; included the Battle of Marengo (1800)
Ended with French victory and the Treaty of Amiens (1802) temporarily breaking coalitions
causes: French expansion under the Directory threatened neighboring monarchies
Resistance to French revolutionary ideals and territorial changes
Formation of shifting alliances against French dominance
outcome: French territorial gains and temporary peace
Coalitions reorganized for future wars against Napoleon
Set stage for Napoleonic Wars and rise of Napoleon as First Consul
impacts: Demonstrated French military innovation under Napoleon
Shifted European alliances and diplomatic patterns
